endonym.gloss: the evening saying of the row-holding

description.value: An account of the first terraces, given by a holder to whoever is standing at the drop with them, usually while waiting for water. It is short, it is not performed, and it ends with an instruction.

content.value:
Before there was a first row there was a first drop, and nobody held it, and the water went where it went.

Somebody stood below it and cut a bench, and the water came to the bench. Somebody stood below that one and cut another. When there were nine, the ninth said: I am ninth. That is the whole of what the ninth said. The ninth did not give a name and did not have one to give. The ninth said where.

Now the ninth is dead and there is a ninth. The ninth owes the fourth two turns of water from the year of the bad wind. The fourth is dead and there is a fourth.

Pay the fourth.
